rule: Pairs come from legal.json related_events only: each event is paired with the earliest later legal item that lists it. Chronology, not causation.

pairs.text: Starfish Prime (1962), then the Limited Test Ban Treaty (1963), which followed it

North Korean jamming of satellite navigation (from 2010), then a 2025 finding by the Assembly of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) on that interference, which the Secure World Foundation also ties to the Baltic case
Shakti destructive test (2019), then UN General Assembly resolution 77/41 (2022), a non-binding call not to conduct destructive anti-satellite tests
Cosmos 1408 destructive test (2021), then a US moratorium on destructive anti-satellite tests (2022), a pledge by the US alone
Interference with satellite navigation around the Baltic Sea (from 2023), then the 2025 ICAO Assembly finding on recurring interference
Jamming of European satellites (2024), then “grave concern” from the Radio Regulations Board of the International Telecommunication Union (2024)

open.text: Laser fired at a satellite (1997): no legal item in our records is related to it
open.basis: No related_events link; the ring states an absence in this ledger, not a finding that no rule exists.

open.text: Viasat cyberattack (2022): the only related legal item, Tallinn Manual 2.0 (2017), is soft law (not binding) and came before the attack
open.basis: tallinn-2017 lists ru-2022-viasat in related_events but is earlier, so it forms no forward pair.
